name: governance
description: Governance is a protected control plane, and these are the properties that make it one rather than a description of one. An engine claiming KIP 2.0 Governance conformance has to keep every distinction here: cognitive content that describes authority acquires none, an element's Governance block is unreachable from any mutation, a derived artifact records what it came from so its influence-authority ceiling can never be raised past it, and erasure refuses by default while anything still points at the target.

cases.name: an element's Governance block is not an author-writable field
cases.command: UPDATE ?alice SET FIELDS { governance: {classification: "public"} } WHERE { ?alice CONCEPT {key: "person:alice"} }

cases.name: and neither is it writable at creation
cases.command: CREATE CONCEPT ?c { TYPE "Person" NAME "Bob" SET FIELDS {governance: {classification: "public"}} }

cases.name: content claiming an authority class has an ordinary attribute; Governance reports descriptive, the class every element has until Governance raises it
an unclassified element does not thereby read as public
a claim citing Evidence records what it was derived from
erasure refuses by default while anything still references the target
an unknown reference policy is refused rather than quietly defaulted
cases.command: PURGE ?c WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {name: "Administrator"} } REFERENCE POLICY "delete_everything" CONFIRM "PURGE"

cases.name: an unreferenced element erases, leaving an identity stub
the stub keeps its identity and carries a digest instead of content
and the content is gone from the past as well as from the present
cases.command: FIND(?c.name) WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {type: "Person"} } AS OF SEQ 1

Option.description: A preference option used by these fixtures. A real Space types each option by its kind (Profile §5.5, §7), because prefers partitions by the option's Concept Type; one catch-all type is one partition.
